approach: Add one reading check, `check_real_records_command(reading, request)`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs`, run as one new `step!` line in `refusing_check` after `check_scope_limit` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It examines each Behavior criterion of a reading that has a capability. A criterion is flagged when it names an athena command and names the real records queue, and has no exemption word and no `--snapshot`. The command forms are `athena <sub>` and `-- <sub>` in a criterion that names athena, for example `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status`. `<sub>` is one of status, plan, queue, drain, retry, go, check-reading, backtest, land. The real-records phrases are `real records`, `records/ queue`, `repository's records`, `repo's records`, `real queue` and `live records`. The exemption words are fixture, temp, tmp, temporary, synthetic and sample. The request exemption is `dependency_ids_in(request)` containing `20261030-070002-d103`, which reads only a 'Depends on' line or the retry link. The error names each flagged criterion by number and text and says to depend on job 20261030-070002-d103 or use a fixture or temp directory. The tests are a new unit test built from the e5sg and sz3z request shapes in `reading.rs`, and new corpus cases. A CHANGELOG entry records the check. No prompt text changes. Root cause: nothing compared the commands a criterion runs with what the producer's and verifier's working copy holds (no `records/`), so criteria that need the real queue were admitted and could not be met. The check sits in the shared gate, not in one reading.

decisions.choice: Matching excludes any criterion that contains `--snapshot`. These criteria are not refused even without a Depends line.
decisions.reason: d103 has already landed. HISTORY.txt:1104 shows commit 823dd32 'Retry job d103: read-only evidence snapshot and athena status --snapshot', and the CHANGELOG describes `status --snapshot` and `crates/athena-core/src/run/records_criteria.rs`, which runs those criteria on the evidence snapshot. `check_records_measure` (surveys.rs:588-596) requires a criterion that names `real records` and tells the reader to write 'Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- status --snapshot <evidence directory>`: on the real records ...'. Existing tests pass such criteria: reading.rs:8350 and 8412-8424 (`REAL_RECORDS_CRITERION`), reading.rs:8563 and 8573 (accepted with gate_refuser None), and refusal_corpus.rs:354 and 441 (Expect Accept). Without the exclusion the new check would contradict that check's own example and break those tests. A `--snapshot` command reads the evidence copy, not records/. The producer's working copy has no `records/` in either form, and `--snapshot` is the d103 mechanism that makes the figures reachable. So this is a matching boundary: the command does not run against the real records/ queue. The Depends-on-d103 line stays the only exemption on the request side.

rejected.option: Refuse every `status`/`plan` criterion that names real records, `--snapshot` included, unless the request depends on d103
rejected.why: It breaks the `check_records_measure` example criterion and about a dozen existing tests and corpus cases, and it contradicts `records_criteria.rs`, which runs those criteria on purpose.

rejected.option: Have the check read records to see whether d103 has landed
rejected.why: Reading checks take no records (the planner and reader copies have none) and the brief puts it out of scope. Admission already holds a job whose Depends on id has not landed: plan.rs:731-737 `unmet_dependency`.

decisions.choice: The check examines Behavior criteria only, and only when `reading.capability` is set. A Content criterion is not examined.
decisions.reason: A Content criterion runs nothing (the `check_records_measure` doc, surveys.rs:522-524, and the test at reading.rs:8444). A docs criterion such as 'the guide says to run `athena status` on the real records' is not an instruction to the producer to run it. `check_criteria_evidence` (surveys.rs:92-94) uses the same `capability.is_none()` gate. Content criteria are covered by a corpus case that must be accepted.

rejected.why: It would flag documentation criteria that only describe the command.

decisions.reason: Existing tests pin the neighbours of several steps: reading.rs:5028-5031 (governance then outcome_state), 5512-5514 (outcome_state then environment_reach), 7535-7537 (environment_reach then defined_terms), 8234-8236 (code_survey then history_fixture) and 8714-8716 (history_fixture then records_measure). Placing the step after check_records_measure keeps reading.rs:8447, 8458 and 8532 correct: they expect `check_records_measure` to refuse first criteria such as 'Run `status` on the real records'. Placing it after scope_limit also keeps the earlier refusers first. Only the position after scope_limit and before boundary has no pinned neighbour (scope_limit_has_one_step_line at reading.rs:8978 only counts lines).

rejected.option: Place it right after check_criteria_evidence, the nearest model check
rejected.why: The 'Run `status` on the real records and show the landing time' criterion (reading.rs:8452-8458) would be refused by the new check, not by the check the test expects.

decisions.choice: Do not change `READING_RULES` (reader.rs:287) or other prompt text, and do not touch briefs.rs, reader.rs or run_pin_tests.rs. The check's error message is the guidance.
decisions.reason: The reader set is at 1998 of 2000 tokens (docs/system-facts.md budgets). briefs.rs pins the rule count at 14 (briefs.rs:4415 and 4855) and the section size at baseline plus two lines (briefs.rs:4483). A new line would break a test or the budget test `system_facts_budgets_match_computed`. The briefs.rs line the brief called a check-name list is a replay-summary test (briefs.rs:4055), unrelated. run_pin_tests.rs uses `check_criteria_evidence` as a fixed rule name (run_pin_tests.rs:2011, 2078), which this change does not alter. The refusal text goes to the reader on the re-read (`read_for`, reading.rs:732-740).

rejected.option: Add a 15th rule line to READING_RULES
rejected.why: It exceeds the reader budget headroom of 2 tokens and breaks pinned counts.

decisions.choice: Command and phrase matching is lexical on normalized text. The text is lowercased with backticks removed and white space squashed; `straight_lowercase` and `has_phrase` in surveys.rs are reused. Command forms: `athena <sub>`, and `-- <sub>` in a criterion that also names athena. Real-records phrases: `real records` (which also matches `real records/`), `records/ queue`, `repository's records`, `repo's records`, `real queue` and `live records`. Exemption words (any one in the criterion): fixture, temp, tmp, temporary, synthetic and sample. The words are taken from a const list in surveys.rs.
decisions.reason: The reading check takes no records and no model. The e5sg shape (from the brief) is 'run athena status on the real records'. The sz3z request text is not in the working copy (records/ is absent), so the sz3z shape is rebuilt from the job brief as an `athena plan` run against 'this repository's records/ queue'. A bare `records/` is not a trigger, so 'records/ is unchanged' or 'no file under records/ changes' is never flagged. `has_phrase` already gives whole-word matching (surveys.rs:39-45).

rejected.why: The brief's own criterion 6 says no file under records/ changes; such statements must stay accepted.

decisions.choice: The dependency exemption calls `dependency_ids_in(request)` (topics.rs:25-60) and compares with `RecordId::parse("20261030-070002-d103")`. It reads only a 'Depends on' line (bullet, number and `>` prefixes stripped, case-insensitive) or the retry link, never a bare mention of the job id.
decisions.reason: Admission holds a job whose Depends on job has not landed (plan.rs:731-737), so the line is the landed condition. A request that only cites d103 (the 'cites-job-without-relying' form) is still refused, because citing a job does not make admission wait for it. The existing retry link also counts: a retry of d103 itself is not blocked.

rejected.option: Accept any request that contains the id text
rejected.why: Admission does not hold the job on a bare mention, so the exemption would be false.

decisions.choice: Exit table for the new check (it is a pure function with no stage, so every exit is `Result`): success/accept: `Ok(())` when the reading has no capability, no Behavior criterion is flagged, or the request depends on d103; the `step!` macro (checks.rs:527-533) continues to the next check. fail: `bail!` with the refusal text; `step!` returns `Some(("check_real_records_command", error))`; `read_for` re-reads once with the text (reading.rs:732-740) and `check_reading_acceptance` returns `Err`. error, hold and interrupt: cannot happen, because the check does no I/O, spawns nothing and takes no lock; a dependency parse failure inside `dependency_ids_in` yields an empty list (topics.rs:33-39 uses `.ok().flatten()`), so it is a refusal, not an error.
decisions.reason: Every exit is the existing step! contract; no new state or record is written, and the stored refusal record carries the rule name as a string (hestia.rs:671-690 groups by rule name).

risks.risk: The sz3z request text and the e5sg text are not in the working copy (records/ is absent), so the shapes are rebuilt from the brief (e5sg: 'run athena status on the real records') and from guesses at the sz3z wording. A real third phrase (for example 'on records/') could slip through.
risks.mitigation: The phrase list also covers `records/ queue`, `repository's records`, `repo's records`, `real queue` and `live records`. Corpus case sources say 'rebuilt from the job brief'. The doc comment states the check is lexical. The replay at verification shows the real effect.

risks.risk: The corpus case readings (docs class, Behavior criterion naming records) may be refused first by an earlier check, such as `check_environment_reach` on records phrases (surveys.rs:792-808, 823, 907), so the new check would not be the refuser.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs the corpus and unit tests and, if an earlier check refuses, adds the `Environment:` assumption to the base reading in that case only. The check's matching is not weakened to avoid it.

risks.risk: A `--snapshot` command that still needs the real records/ queue is not flagged, so one form of the original fault remains.
risks.mitigation: That form is Athena's own `records_criteria.rs` path and has the evidence snapshot (d103 landed, HISTORY.txt:1104). The doc comment names the boundary.

risks.risk: The refusal rate rises more than the 3% estimate, or the exemption words (sample, temp) let a real-records criterion through.
risks.mitigation: The share is declared as an estimate; the verification replay measures it and holds the job above 10% unless declared. The exemption list is short and whole-word.

risks.risk: Placing a check between existing steps changes which rule name a mixed reading is refused by.
risks.mitigation: The position was chosen from the pinned neighbours listed in dependents. The full `cargo test --locked` run covers the rest.

demonstrations.method: The unit test builds a docs reading from `governed_reading` and `add_behavior` (reading.rs:4647 and 4794), whose Behavior criterion is 'Run `athena status` on the real records and report the landed jobs'. It calls `check_real_records_command(&reading, request)`. Without a Depends line it asserts the error contains 'criterion 1', the criterion text, 'Depends on 20261030-070002-d103' or '20261030-070002-d103', and 'fixture'. Then the request gets a 'Depends on 20261030-070002-d103' line (in a dash bullet, a `1.` part and plain text) and the same reading is accepted. A request that only says '20261030-070002-d103 landed' stays refused. A request with 'Depends on 20260101-000000-abcd' (another job) stays refused. This also shows that the dependency is the only request exemption.
